p0.original: 关键问题：社会系统如何塑造影响行为的情境
p0.en: Key issue: How social systems shape the context that shapes behaviour

p2.original: 社会系统会影响情境，而情境会影响行为。通过理解社会系统，我们就可以学习如何优化它，同时消除其所造成的负面影响。
p2.en: Social systems affect situations that affect behaviour. By understanding the social system, we can learn how to optimize it while eliminating its negative effects.

p3.original: 我们一生中的大部分时间都在各种机构中度过，如家庭、学校、医院、工作场所、军队、监狱、养老院，最后可能会住进临终收容所。每种环境都包含管控系统、清晰或隐含的行为准则、奖惩措施，它们拥有完整的历史、文化和法律。在许多情况下，正是这种体制力量创造、维持了社会环境，并赋予其意义和合理性。体制力量（system power）与群体内部的社会规范不同，因为它通过制度化或合法化的系统运作，自上而下地对群体和个人进行控制。尽管社会心理学家强调了情境对行为的影响，但他们并不认为系统有更强大的力量能让这些情境发挥作用，这些作用时好时坏。这就引出了本章的下一个核心概念：
p3.en: Most of our lives have been spent in institutions such as homes, schools, hospitals, workplaces, the army, prisons, homes for the elderly and, eventually, in penitentiaries. Each environment contains a regulatory system, a clear or implicit code of conduct, incentives and sanctions, and they have a complete history, culture and law. In many cases, it is this institutional force that creates, sustains, gives meaning and legitimacy to the social environment. Institutional forces (system power) are different from social norms within the group, as they operate through institutionalized or legalized systems to control groups and individuals from the top down. While social psychologists have highlighted the effects of situations on behaviour, they do not believe that the system has stronger forces to make these situations work, which are sometimes good and bad. This leads to the next core concept of this chapter:

p4.original: 社会系统会影响情境，而情境会影响行为。通过理解社会系统，我们就可以学习如何优化它，同时消除其造成的负面影响。
p4.en: Social systems affect situations that affect behaviour. By understanding the social system, we can learn how to optimize it while eliminating its negative effects.

p5.original: 我们将在斯坦福监狱实验（Stanford Prison Experiment，SPE）中说明体制力量是如何创造强大的社会情境，并在情境中影响所有人的行为的。然后，我们将简要地研究一些同样产生了虐待行为的系统，例如，伊拉克的阿布格莱布监狱。在本章中，我们没有足够的篇幅来详细说明系统是如何运作以产生好结果的。就像那些参与大多数非暴力运动的人，例如，印度的甘地、美国民权斗争中的马丁·路德·金以及南非反对种族隔离制度的纳尔逊·曼德拉训练公民被动抵抗。基督教徒和其他人帮助犹太人逃离纳粹大屠杀时，类似的系统网络也至关重要。
p5.en: In the Stanford Prison Experiment (Standford Prison Exchange, SPE), we will show how institutional forces create a strong social context and influence the behaviour of all people in that context. We will then briefly study some systems that have also produced abuses, such as the Abu Ghraib prison in Iraq. In this chapter, we do not have enough space to detail how the system works to produce good results. Like those involved in most non-violent movements, such as Gandhi in India, Martin Luther King in the civil rights struggle in the United States and Nelson Mandela in South Africa against apartheid, who trained passive resistance from citizens. Similar systemic networks are also crucial when Christians and others help Jews escape the Holocaust.

p12.en: A description of the results of the Stanford prison experiment.

p13.original: 在加利福尼亚一个夏日的星期天，一声警报打破了大学生汤米·惠特洛（Tommy Whitlow）的宁静的清晨。一辆城市警车嘎吱一声停在他家门前。几分钟后，警方指控汤米犯有重罪，并告知他现在拥有的宪法权利，之后对其进行搜身后并戴上了手铐。在市立监狱进行登记并采集指纹后，汤米被蒙上眼睛，并被押送到斯坦福县监狱。在那里，他的衣服被脱光，并获得了一套罩衫式的制服，正反面都有他的身份号码。汤米成了“第8612号囚犯”。当地警方还逮捕了另外8名大学生，并分配了编号。
p13.en: On a summer Sunday in California, an alarm broke the quiet morning of a university student, Tommy Whitlow. An urban police car squeaked in front of his house. A few minutes later, the police charged Tommy with a felony and informed him of his current constitutional rights, after which he was searched and handcuffed. After registration and fingerprinting at the municipal prison, Tommy was blindfolded and taken to Stanford County Prison. There, his clothes were stripped off and he was given a uniform in the form of a hoodie with his identity number on his back. Tommy became “Personal Prison No. 8612”. The local police also arrested and assigned numbers to eight other university students.

p14.original: 狱警们身着卡其色军装，戴着反光太阳镜，他们没有透露自己的姓名，只有“狱警先生”的身份标识，但他们的大警棍、哨子和手铐表明了他们的权力。对他们来说，没有权力的囚犯只不过是毫无价值的数字。
p14.en: The guards were wearing khaki-coloured military uniforms, mirrors, they did not reveal their names, only the identification of “Mr. Prisoner”, but their batons, whistles and handcuffs demonstrated their authority. For them, prisoners without power are no more than worthless figures.

p15.original: 狱警们要求囚犯们完全遵守他们任意制定的所有规则。如果有人质疑并反抗，就会失去某些“特权”。起初，这些“特权”包括阅读、写字或与其他囚犯交谈。后来，哪怕他们只是窃窃私语，也会导致他们失去吃饭、睡觉、洗澡和被探视的“特权”。囚犯们不遵守规则时，还被迫做各种令人讨厌的任务，例如，没完没了的俯卧撑、跳跃运动和连续数小时的报数。每天狱警对囚犯的敌意虐待都在升级：让他们徒手清洁厕所，被狱警踩在后背上做俯卧撑，长时间裸着身体被单独监禁，最后被进行有辱人格的性羞辱。
p15.en: The prison guards demanded that the prisoners comply fully with all the rules they had set at their disposal. If anyone questions and resists, certain “privileges” are lost. Initially, these “privileges” included reading, writing or talking to other prisoners. Later, even if they were just whispering, they would lose their “privileges” to eat, sleep, bathe and be visited. Prisoners are also forced to perform odious tasks when they do not comply with the rules, such as endless push-ups, jumping exercises and counting for hours. The hostile ill-treatment of prisoners by prison guards is escalating daily: they are cleaning toilets with their bare hands, they are trampled on their backs by prison guards, they are kept in solitary confinement naked for prolonged periods of time, and they are finally subjected to degrading sexual humiliation.

p16.original: “第8612号囚犯”遇到的一些狱警，对他和其他囚犯的行为都有虐待倾向，显然以虐待他们为乐；另一些狱警仅仅是态度很强硬，要求苛刻；少数狱警没有虐待行为。然而，没有一个“好”狱警曾质疑过“作恶者”极端贬低囚犯的行为。
p16.en: (b) The ill-treatment of some prison guards who were met by “prisoner 8612”, who were all tending to abuse him and other prisoners, apparently with a view to their abuse; Other prison guards are simply tough and demanding; A few prison guards did not commit ill-treatment. However, no “good” prison guard has questioned the extreme derogatory behaviour of the “perpetrators”.

p17.original: 在大规模逮捕后不到36小时，“第8612号囚犯”因为产生极度紧张的反应（尖叫、哭泣、愤怒和抑郁）而被迫释放。他是那天早上发生的一场未遂的囚犯叛乱的头目。连续几天，又有3名囚犯出现了类似的压力相关症状。第5名囚犯在假释委员会驳回他的上诉后由于心理压力而全身起了皮疹，便也被释放了。图11-14是来自这个著名实验的一些原始照片。
p17.en: Less than 36 hours after the mass arrest, “prisoner 8612” was forced to be released because of extremely stressful reactions (screams, cries, anger and depression). He was the leader of an attempted prisoner rebellion that morning. Three more prisoners experienced similar stress-related symptoms over several consecutive days. The fifth prisoner was also released after having been subjected to psychological stress as a result of the dismissal of his appeal by the Parole Board. Figures 11-14 are some of the original photographs from this famous experiment.

p18.original: 11.10.1 是什么导致了斯坦福监狱实验中的行为
p18.en: 11.10.1 What led to the behaviour of Stanford Prison Experiment?

p19.original: 无论是狱警还是囚犯都是从一大批学生志愿者中挑选出来的。这些志愿者通过全面的心理测试和访谈，均为遵纪守法、情绪稳定、身体健康、人格特质指标为正常水平的人。在这个模拟监狱实验中，被试被随机分配到“狱警”或“囚犯”两种角色中。因此，在实验一开始，扮演囚犯或狱警这两种不同实验角色的男性大学生之间并没有显著差异。而研究结束时，这两个群体之间已经有了显著差异。囚犯们24小时生活在监狱里，狱警则每天按8小时标准轮班。监狱“主管”是这个研究的主要研究员，也是本书的作者之一——菲利普·津巴多。
p19.en: Both prison guards and prisoners were selected from among a large number of student volunteers. Through comprehensive psychological tests and interviews, these volunteers are those who are in compliance with the law, emotional stability, physical health, and personal qualities. In this simulation of the prison, they were randomly assigned to the roles of “prisoners” or “prisoners”. Thus, at the beginning of the experiment, there was no significant difference between male students who played the two different experimental roles of prisoner or prison guard. At the end of the study, there were significant differences between the two groups. Prisoners live 24 hours in prison, while prison guards work in shifts of eight hours a day. The prison “supervisor” was the main researcher and one of the authors of the book, Philip Zimbabwe.

p20.original: 那些在日常生活中曾是和平主义者和“好人”的学生在扮演狱警时表现得具有攻击性，甚至做出残暴的虐待行为。心理稳定的学生扮演囚犯时很快就表现出病态行为，产生习得性无助（learned helolessness），屈服于这种命运。模拟监狱情境的力量在狱警和他们的俘虏的内心创造了一个新的社会现实——一个具有真实功能的监狱。实验情况变得令人十分不安，研究人员仅仅在6天后就被迫终止了本应为期2周的研究。
p20.en: Students who were pacifists and “good people” in their daily lives behaved aggressively and even brutally as prison guards. Students who are mentally stable quickly behaved as prisoners, producing a learned helolessness, and giving in to this fate. The power of simulation of prison conditions creates a new social reality in the hearts of prison guards and their prisoners — a prison with real functions. The experiment became very disturbing, and the researchers were forced to terminate the research, which was supposed to last two weeks, after only six days.

p21.original: 图11-14 来自津巴多斯坦福监狱实验的图片
p21.en: Figure 11-14. Picture from Zimbabwe Stanford Prison Experiment

p22.original: 尽管惠特洛说他不想再次经历这一切了，但他很珍惜这段个人经历，因为这让他对自己和人性有了更多的了解。幸运的是，他和其他学生基本上都很健康，大量的报告显示，他们已经从监狱经历中恢复过来。经过多年的跟踪调查，没有发现实验对这些学生产生持久的负面影响。所有的被试都学到了重要的一课：永远不要低估糟糕情境的力量以及创造这种情境的体制力量，它们能破坏那些最优秀和最聪明的人的人格和良好教养。
p22.en: Although Whitlow said he did not want to go through all of this again, he valued that personal experience, which gave him a better understanding of himself and of humanity. Fortunately, he and other students were generally healthy and there were numerous reports indicating that they had recovered from prison experience. After many years of follow-up, no lasting negative effects of the experiment on these students were found. All of the tests have learned an important lesson: never underestimate the power of bad situations and the institutional power to create them, which can undermine the integrity and well-educated of the best and brightest.

p23.original: 澳大利亚的一项跨文化研究重复了这项实验，并得出了类似的结果（Lovibond et al，1979）。然而，可能是因为澳大利亚的研究遵循了每个人都享有下午茶的文化规范，所以从来没有警官表现出如斯坦福监狱实验那样的暴力程度！关于这项戏剧性研究及许多相关问题的详细信息，读者可自行在网上搜索。
p23.en: An intercultural study in Australia repeated the experiment and produced similar results (Lovibond et al. 1979). However, perhaps because the Australian study followed the cultural norms of tea for everyone, police officers never showed the level of violence that Stanford had experimented with! Readers can search online for detailed information on this dramatic study and many related issues.

p24.original: 假如你是斯坦福监狱实验中的其中一个被试，你会变成一个好狱警，还是虐待狂？你会做一个遵纪守法的模范囚犯，还是反叛者？你能承受住这些环境的压力吗？
p24.en: If you're one of those Stanford prison tests, will you be a good prison guard or a sadist? Will you be a law-abiding prisoner or a rebel? Can you withstand the pressure of these environments?

p25.original: 类似的问题在米尔格拉姆服从实验中也可能被提出，如果你是这个实验中的被试，你认为自己会如何表现——服从还是反抗？我们都愿意相信自己将会是优秀的狱警和英勇的囚犯，永远不会越过善与恶的界线。当然，我们都相信自己能够正确地看待事物，知道这“只是一个实验”，只是角色扮演，并不是真实的。但最可能的情况是，大多数人的反应会和这些被试一样。这项令人不安的研究提出了许多问题，这些问题涉及我们对自己、对内在性格品质有多少了解，以及对外部的微妙力量又有多少了解。显然，这也引发了伦理问题，我们是否应该继续进行这样的研究？
p25.en: A similar question may be raised in the Milgram Subordination experiment, and if you were tested in this experiment, how do you think you would behave — obey or resist? We are all willing to believe that we will be good prison guards and brave prisoners and that we will never cross the line between good and evil. Of course, we all believe that we can see things right, knowing that it is “an experiment”, but role-playing, not real. But most likely, most people will react the same way they were tried. This disturbing study raises many questions about how much we know about ourselves, how much we know about the quality of the inner character and how much about the subtle forces of the outside. Clearly, it also raises ethical questions, and should we continue such research?

p26.original: 11.10.2 斯坦福监狱实验的结果如何
p26.en: 11.10.2 What's the results of Stanford Prison Experiment?

p27.original: 斯坦福监狱实验的结论表明，狱警和囚犯的行为在各个可见的方面都是不同的（见图11-15）。然而，这只是偶然的，因为他们的角色是随机分配的——这些角色创造了地位和权力的差异，而这些差异在类似监狱情境中得到了证实，并得到了监狱实验权威系统的支持。
p27.en: The conclusions of the Stanford prison experiment show that the behaviour of prison guards and prisoners varies in all visible respects (see figure 11-15). However, it is only by chance, because their roles are randomly assigned — these create differences in status and power, which are confirmed in similar prison situations and supported by the system of experimental authority in prisons.

p28.original: 图11-15 SPE中的狱警和囚犯的行为
p28.en: The behaviour of prison guards and prisoners in SPE, Figure 11-15

p29.original: 注：你可以看见实验中狱警和囚犯的极端行为差异。
p29.en: Note: You can see extreme behaviour differences between prison guards and prisoners in the experiment.

p30.original: 没有人教被试如何扮演某些角色。在没有参观过真正的监狱的情况下，所有的被试在之前的生活中已经了解了有权势的人和平民之间的互动方式。狱警通过限制囚犯的自由来管理他们的行为，让他们的行为可以更好地被预测。狱警还通过制定强制性的规则进行管理，其中包括对违规行为的惩罚。囚犯只能对权力者创造的监狱环境中的社会结构做出一些反应。他们只能选择反抗或服从，第一种选择导致惩罚，而第二种选择则导致丧失自主性和尊严。
p30.en: No one teaches how to be tested in some roles. In the absence of a visit to a real prison, all the people who had been tried had learned about the way in which powerful people interacted with civilians in their previous lives. Prison guards regulate the behaviour of prisoners by restricting their freedom and making their behaviour more predictable. The prison guards are also administered through the establishment of mandatory rules, which include penalties for violations. Prisoners can only respond to the social structure of the prison environment created by the power-bearers. They can only choose to resist or obey, the first leads to punishment, while the second leads to loss of autonomy and dignity.

p31.original: 参与实验的学生在以前的许多社会互动中已经经历过由各种控制系统所形成的权力差异，如亲子、师生、医患、老板和员工、男性和女性。他们只是在特定的环境下完善和强化了以前的行为模式。每个学生都可以扮演任何一个角色。许多扮演狱警的学生报告说，他们对自己如此容易地就享受控制别人这件事而感到惊讶。最冷漠、残酷的“狱警”后来在一部电视纪录片中回忆说，狱警就像操控木偶戏的表演者一样，拉着绑在囚犯身上的绳子，并在此过程中“寻欢作乐”。仅仅穿上制服就足以将他们从被动的大学生转变为好斗的狱警。
p31.en: Students involved in the experiment have experienced power differentials resulting from various control systems, such as parents, teachers and students, medical patients, employers and employees, men and women, in many of the previous social interactions. They have only perfected and reinforced previous patterns of behaviour in specific contexts. Every student can play any role. Many of the students who played the role of prison guards reported that they were surprised that they enjoyed control so easily. The coldest and cruelest “prisoners” later recalled in a television documentary that prison guards, like performers who manipulated puppet scenes, pulled ropes tied to prisoners and, in the process, “had fun”. A uniform alone would suffice to transform them from passive university students to militant prison guards.

p32.original: 11.10.3 比较米尔格拉姆与斯坦福监狱的实验研究
p32.en: 11.10.3 Experimental study comparing Millgram and Stanford prisons

p33.original: 米尔格拉姆的服从研究和斯坦福监狱实验成了许多研究的佐证，说明了情境对行为的影响。然而，服从研究是关于个人权威的权力，而监狱实验是关于制度的权力，一个统治系统的权力。狱警保持着虐待的状态，心理学家的研究团队也是如此。警察和许多到过监狱的人都促成了这一事实，如监狱牧师、公设辩护律师、来探访的父母和朋友，以及假释委员会的平民。在2015年，这个经典的社会心理学实验被拍摄成获奖故事片（见图11-16）。
p33.en: Milgram's obedience study and Stanford prison experiments were supported by many studies on the effects of the situation on behaviour. However, subjection to the study is about the power of the individual, while the prison experiment is about the power of the system, the power of the ruling system. Prison guards maintained a state of ill-treatment, as did the research team of psychologists. The police and many people who have been to prison contribute to this fact, such as prison pastors, public defenders, visiting parents and friends, and civilians on parole boards. In 2015, this classic socio-psychological experiment was filmed as a winning feature film (see figures 11-16).

p40.original: 解释社会系统在理解人类行为中如何发挥作用。
p40.en: Explain how social systems work in understanding human behaviour.

p41.original: 心理学家试图理解各种行为，以更好地促进亲社会行为，以及转变反社会行为。理解为什么有些人会从事“不良行为”，这并不是为他们找借口，而是为了更好地改变对这些行为产生影响的思想。对最复杂的人类行为的全面理解应该包括对高阶因素（即权力系统）如何创造和塑造情境条件的理解。要理解复杂的行为模式，就必须考虑系统，而不仅仅是人格特质和情境。
p41.en: Psychologists try to understand behaviour to better promote pro-social behaviour and to transform anti-social behaviour. It is not an excuse to understand why some people are engaging in “bad behaviour”, but rather to better change the mindsets that affect them. A comprehensive understanding of the most complex human behaviour should include an understanding of how high-level factors (i.e. power systems) create and shape the conditions of the situation. To understand complex patterns of behaviour, systems must be considered, not just personality characteristics and circumstances.

p42.original: 在服务行业，如警察、狱警或士兵，甚至在商业环境中，个人反常、违法或不道德行为通常会被贴上“几个坏苹果”的标签。这意味着他们只是罕见的例外，在善与恶之间，有一条不可逾越的界线，少数坏苹果被置于界限的一边，而大多数好苹果则被置于另一边。但是谁来进行区分呢？通常是系统的守护者，他们想要孤立问题，转移公众对高层人士的注意，他们可能要为创造了这种环境或缺乏监督负责任。同样，关注坏苹果者的个人特性忽略了关注装坏苹果的桶的情境或潜在影响。对系统的分析使我们关注一个更高的层级——坏桶的制造者，即系统的视角，也就是那些有能力设计桶的人。正是那些“权力精英”（桶的制造者）在幕后发挥作用，为其他人设置了许多生活条件，而我们必须在他们所构建的各种制度环境中生活。
p42.en: In the service industry, such as police, prison guards or soldiers, and even in a commercial environment, individual abnormal, illegal or immoral behaviour is usually labelled as “a few bad apples”. This means that they are only rare exceptions, and there is an insurmountable line between good and evil, with a few bad apples being placed on one side of the line, while most good apples are placed on the other. But who's gonna make the difference? Often system custodians, who want to isolate problems and divert public attention from high-level individuals who may be responsible for creating such an environment or for lack of oversight. Similarly, attention to the personal characteristics of bad apples ignores the context or potential impact of the drums containing bad apples. An analysis of the system has focused our attention on a higher level — the manufacturer of the bad barrel — that is, the perspective of the system, that is, those who are capable of designing the barrel. It is those “power elites” (the barrel makers) who have played a role behind the scenes and have set many living conditions for others, and we must live in the institutional environments that they have built.

p44.original: 从本节的核心概念中我们可以学到的最重要的一课是，系统创造了情境。系统提供体制上的支持、权威和资源，使情境能够按照它们的方式运行。体制力量（system power）涉及授权或制度化的许可，以规定的方式行事，禁止和惩罚不被认可的行为。它提供了“更高的权威”，对扮演新角色、遵守新规则以及采取通常会受到现有法律、规范、道德和伦理约束的行动给予了认可。这种确认通常披着意识形态的外衣。意识形态是一种口号或主张，通常让实现最终目标的一切手段合法化。为支持一种意识形态而开发的程序、政策和标准操作程序是系统的基本组成部分。由于意识形态被认为是神圣的，因此该系统的程序也被认为是合理且适当的。
p44.en: The most important lesson we can learn from the core concepts of this section is that the system creates the situation. The system provides institutional support, authority and resources to enable situations to function in their way. Institutional power (system power) involves authorization or institutionalized authorization to act in a prescribed manner and to prohibit and punish unacknowledged acts. It provides “higher authority” and recognizes new roles, adherence to new rules and actions that are usually subject to existing laws, norms, ethics and ethics. Such confirmation is often in the guise of ideology. Ideology is a slogan or proposition that often legitimizes all means of achieving the ultimate goal. The procedures, policies and standard operating procedures developed to support an ideology are essential components of the system. Since ideology is considered sacred, the system's procedures are also considered reasonable and appropriate.

p45.original: 然而，尽管所有的系统都涉及不同权力和地位的个体，但大多数系统都不透明；也就是说，系统通常会对外界隐藏其大部分运作。因此，即使一个系统未能达到其宗旨和目标，就像许多失败的教育或惩教系统（以及存在腐败行为的公司）一样，其高层人士也不会受到公众的审查。
p45.en: However, while all systems involve individuals with different powers and status, most systems are not transparent; In other words, systems usually hide most of their operations from the outside world. Thus, even if a system fails to achieve its goals and objectives, as is the case with many failed educational or correctional systems (and companies that have corrupt practices), its senior members will not be subject to public scrutiny.

p46.original: 不过，当情况可能是错误的时候，要想改变不良行为并促进更符合社会的行为，仅依靠个人治疗模式（或管教个体）来解决问题行为是不够的。改善现状的计划必须涉及对创建和维护现状的系统的理解和修改。同时，我们呼吁采用公共卫生模式，将个人的痛苦和疾病视为社会疾病传播的后果。将预防而不仅仅是治疗作为目标，接种疫苗可预防流行病的传播。对于社会中的偏见、暴力和霸凌也应该像对病毒感染一样。系统的力量可以影响个人行为，其中一个比较著名的例子发生在10年前的伊拉克阿布格莱布（Abu Ghraib）美军监狱。
p46.en: However, when circumstances may be wrong, it is not enough to rely on individual treatment models (or individual discipline) to address the behaviour in question in order to change the behaviour and promote more socially appropriate behaviour. Plans to improve the status quo must involve understanding and modification of the systems that create and maintain the status quo. At the same time, we call for a public health model that treats individual suffering and disease as a consequence of the spread of social diseases. With prevention as a goal, not just treatment, vaccinations can prevent the spread of the epidemic. Prejudice, violence and bullying in society should be the same as infection with the virus. One of the more famous examples of the power of the system that can influence individual behaviour occurred 10 years ago in Abu Ghraib, Iraq, at the United States military prison.

p47.original: 11.11.2 用心理学来解释阿布格莱布监狱的虐待行为
p47.en: 11.11.2 Psychological interpretation of abuse in Abu Ghraib prison

p48.original: 在三个月的时间里，服役于阿布格莱布监狱地牢的1-A层值夜班的宪兵、陆军预备役军人，将被关押在那里的1000名囚犯中的一些人当作他们的“玩物”，将他们一丝不挂地堆成金字塔状，把女人的内裤倒着戴在他们的头上，用狗链拖着他们在地上走来走去，用各种方式对他们进行性侮辱。1-A层是由军事情报部门、中央情报局和一个平民审讯承包商管理的审讯中心。当针对美军的意外叛乱突然升级时，指挥系统需要从这些被拘留者那里获得有效的情报。因此，国会议员的监狱看守得到了上级的许可，可以“软化”囚犯，让他们为审讯做好准备。
p48.en: For three months, military police and army reservists on the 1-A night shift in the dungeon of Abu Ghraib prison treated some of the 1,000 prisoners held there as “players”, folding them into pyramids naked, putting women's underwear upside down on their heads, dragging them around the ground with dog chains, and sexually insulting them in various ways. Level 1-A is an interrogation centre run by the Military Intelligence, the Central Intelligence Agency and a civilian interrogation contractor. When the unexpected rebellion against the United States forces suddenly escalated, the chain of command required effective information from the detainees. As a result, prison guards of members of Parliament have received permission from their superiors to “soft” prisoners to prepare them for trial.

p49.original: 有了官方的虐待许可，而且在没有高级警官监督或监视夜班的情况下，一切都乱套了。然而，士兵们并不认为他们这样做不对，其中一人说，这只是“娱乐和游戏”。实际上，他们用照片坦率地记录了这些“游戏”，并以数百张恐怖的照片记录了自己与受虐囚徒的关系。
p49.en: With official authorization for ill-treatment, and without supervision or supervision of night work by senior police officers, everything is in disarray. However, the soldiers did not think that they were doing it wrong, and one of them said that it was merely “recreational and play”. In fact, they frankly recorded these “plays” with photographs and their relationship with the abused prisoners with hundreds of horror photographs.

p50.original: 阿布格莱布监狱的士兵们拍摄了1000多张照片，记录了他们虐待和侮辱伊拉克囚犯的行为。
p50.en: The soldiers of Abu Ghraib prison took over 1,000 photographs documenting their ill-treatment and humiliation of Iraqi prisoners.

p51.original: 一个由前国防部长詹姆斯·施莱辛格（James Schlesinger）领导的调查委员会成立，其成员包括将军和其他高级官员。他们在报告中指出，社会心理学的研究和理论对理解这些虐待行为的重要性。
p51.en: A commission of inquiry led by former Minister of Defence James Schlesinger, including generals and other senior officials, was established. In the report, they noted the importance of psychosocial research and theory in understanding these abuses.

p52.original: 基于对社会心理学原理的基本理解以及对许多已知环境风险因素的认识，全球反恐战争期间被拘留者遭受虐待的可能性是完全可以预测的……社会心理学领域的研究结果表明，战争状况和被拘留者的动力学系统具有引发虐待的内在风险，因此必须格外谨慎，并对此进行仔细的规划和训练。
p52.en: Based on a basic understanding of the philosophy of social psychology and an understanding of the many known environmental risk factors, the potential for abuse of detainees during the global war on terror is entirely predictable... Research in the social psychology field suggests that war conditions and the detainee's kinetic system are intrinsically at risk of causing ill-treatment, and therefore require extra care and careful planning and training.

p53.original: 即使某些条件会增加虐待的可能性，但故意从事不道德或非法行为的个人是无法得到原谅和赦免的。
p53.en: Even if certain conditions increase the likelihood of ill-treatment, individuals who deliberately engage in immoral or unlawful acts cannot be forgiven or pardoned.

p54.original: 《施莱辛格报告》（Schlesinger Report）大胆宣称：“斯坦福大学一项具有里程碑意义的研究为所有军事拘留行为提供了一个警示。”通过对比斯坦福监狱实验中相对温和的环境，该报告明确指出，“在军事拘留行动中，士兵在紧张且不良的战斗环境下工作。”这意味着，相比我们在模拟监狱实验中所观察到的，这些战斗条件可能会催生更为极端的狱警滥用权力的行为。《施莱辛格报告》的结论强调了我们在本章中讲述的许多内容：“心理学家试图理解，通常表现出人道主义的个人和群体，为何有时会在特定情况下做出不人道的行为。”该报告阐述了一些概念，有助于解释为什么虐待行为会发生在一般表现为人道主义的个体中，这些概念包括去个性化、非人化、敌对形象、群体思维、道德脱离、社会助长和其他环境因素。
p54.en: The Schlesinger Report boldly declared: “A landmark study at Stanford University provides a warning for all military detentions. Through the relatively mild environment in the Bistanfu prison experiment, the report clearly states that “in military detention operations soldiers work in a tense and hostile combat environment. This means that these combat conditions may lead to more extreme abuses by prison guards than we have observed in the mock prison experiment. The conclusions of the Schlesinger report highlight many of the elements we have described in this chapter: “Physicians try to understand why individuals and groups who usually manifest humanitarianism sometimes commit inhumane acts in specific circumstances. The report sets out concepts that help to explain why abuses occur in individuals who generally manifest themselves in a humanitarian context, such as depersonalization, dehumanization, hostile images, group thinking, moral isolation, social promotion and other environmental factors.

p55.original: 比起这份官方的政府报告，我们知道的直接强调心理学理论和社会心理学研究价值的官方陈述更少。完整的报告对心理学学生来说很重要，特别是附录G。
p55.en: We know less than this official government report of official statements that directly emphasize the value of psychological theory and psychosocial research. Full reports are important for students of psychology, especially Appendix G.

p56.original: 通过用社会心理学分析普通男女（狱警）对其他普通男女（战俘）的虐待行为，说明了应用心理学概念来理解复杂的个人、情境和系统行为的价值。
p56.en: The value of applying the concept of psychology to understand complex personal, contextual and systemic behaviour is illustrated by the psychopsychological analysis of the abuse of men and women (prisoners) by other men and women (prisoners of war).

p57.original: 11.12 通过系统化的改变和重构来防止霸凌
p57.en: 11.12 Prevention of Bullying through Systemic Changes and Reconstruction

p59.original: 回顾霸凌的不良影响和防止霸凌的方法。
p59.en: Recall the negative effects of bullying and ways to prevent it.

p60.original: 学校和工作场所的霸凌（bullying）主要是一些学生和员工通过极端的戏弄、威胁、身体虐待和通过谎言、流言蜚语破坏他人的声誉，使他人的生活变得痛苦不堪（见图11-17）。大多数学生和员工既不是霸凌者也不是受害者，而是意识到问题的旁观者，但他们通常会忽略或被动地接受它（Coloroso，2008）。针对恃强凌弱者，传统的方法是找出他们并用各种方式惩罚他们，把他们调到其他班级、学校或工作岗位。这可能会将施暴者及其虐待行为转移到不同的场所，但并不会改变他们。通常，这会让他们更加愤怒，更想报复。霸凌被定义为系统且长期地对他人造成身体伤害或心理困扰，无论他们是学生还是员工。
p60.en: The bullying in schools and workplaces is mainly the result of extreme harassment, threats, physical abuse and the destruction of the reputation of others through lies and rumours (see figure 11-17). The majority of students and employees are neither bullies nor victims, but bystanders who are aware of the problem, but they usually ignore or passively accept it (Coloroso, 2008). The traditional approach for the bullying is to find them and punish them in various ways and transfer them to other classes, schools or jobs. This may transfer perpetrators and their abuse to different settings, but it does not change them. Usually, it makes them more angry and more anxious to take revenge. Bullying is defined as the systematic and long-term infliction of bodily harm or psychological distress on others, whether they are students or employees.

p61.original: 图11-17 报告的霸凌类型

p62.original: 注：在许多场合，霸凌行为以各种形式出现。
p62.en: Note: In many instances, bullying takes place in various forms.

p63.original: 在20世纪90年代，有关霸凌行为的统计数据显示，瑞典的霸凌现象相对较少，据估计，有15%的瑞典学龄儿童表示曾受到霸凌或承认自己是霸凌者（Olweus，1993）。然而，最近的一项调查显示，在英国，霸凌现象的比例显著升高，英国人口样本中有73%的被试报告说自己被霸凌过，是霸凌者，或者直接目睹过霸凌（McLeod，2008）。这项大规模的研究调查了14所学校中近2000名12至19岁的学生。2010年一项针对43000名美国高中生的调查显示，有一半的人说他们在过去的一年中曾欺负过别人，近一半的人说他们曾遭受身体虐待、嘲笑或被以一种令他们感到严重不安的方式嘲弄（Dalton，2010）。在霸凌的负面影响中，估计有16万名学生因为可能受到同龄人的身体和言语攻击而拒绝上学。
p63.en: Statistics on bullying in the 1990s show that bullying in Sweden was relatively low, with an estimated 15 per cent of Swedish school-age children indicating that they had been bullied or admitted to being bullies (Olweus, 1993). However, a recent survey shows that bullying rates have increased significantly in the United Kingdom, where 73 per cent of the sample population has been tried to report that they have been bullied, are bullies or have witnessed bullying directly (McLeod, 2008). This large-scale study surveyed nearly 2,000 students aged 12 to 19 in 14 schools. A 2010 survey of 43,000 high school students in the United States showed that half of them said they had bullied others in the past year, and nearly half said that they had been physically abused, ridiculed or mocked in a way that seriously upsets them (Dalton, 2010). Among the negative effects of bullying, an estimated 160,000 students refuse to attend school because they may be physically and verbally assaulted by their peers.

p64.original: 11.12.1 如今的霸凌是什么样子的

p65.original: 以下是最常见的霸凌类型。
p65.en: The most common types of bullying are listed below.

p66.original: 身体霸凌：通过打、推、挤、踢、掐或按住他人来实施直接的身体暴力。身体霸凌还包括拿走或打碎别人的财物，偷窃或勒索金钱。
p66.en: Physical bullying: Direct physical violence by beating, pushing, squeezing, kicking, choking or holding others hostage. Physical bullying also includes taking or breaking other people's belongings, stealing or extorting money.

p67.original: 言语霸凌：用言语伤害别人，包括威胁、嘲弄、恐吓、侮辱、讽刺、辱骂、戏弄、污辱、涂鸦、奚落和嘲笑。它还包括敌对动作，如做鬼脸、凝视、瞪眼、翻白眼和吐痰。
p67.en: Intimidation of speech: The use of words to harm others, including threats, ridicule, intimidation, insults, sarcasm, insults, insults, graffiti, scorn and ridicule. It also includes hostile actions, such as face-to-face, stare, eye-to-eye, white eyes and spit.

p68.original: 关系霸凌：将某人排除在群体之外或故意挤对他，说闲话、戏弄、窃窃私语并散布谣言，包括背弃他人，漠视他人，排斥他人或找替罪羊。
p68.en: Relationship bullying: To exclude or deliberately squeeze a person from a group, to gossip, to tease, to whisper and spread rumours, including turning away from others, ignoring others, excluding others or finding scapegoats.

p69.original: 网络霸凌：使用手机、短信、电子邮件、即时消息、网络博客和发帖子等方式霸凌另一个学生。网络霸凌的例子包括通过电话和电子邮件发送威胁或侮辱性的信息，以及散播破坏性的谣言，破坏一个同学或同事的声誉。
p69.en: Internet bullying: bullying another student using mobile phones, text messages, e-mails, instant messaging, web blogs and postings. Examples of cyber bullying include sending threatening or insulting messages via telephone and e-mail, and spreading destructive rumours that undermine the reputation of a fellow student or colleague.

p70.original: 骚扰：具有攻击性和可能具有威胁性的行为，包括使用极端的口头语言、攻击性的问题或陈述、跟踪、身体暴力或性侵犯。性骚扰是持续的、不受欢迎的性侵犯，拒绝的话可能会对受害者造成伤害。通常骚扰是重复的行为，但并非总是如此。
p70.en: Harassment: offensive and potentially threatening behaviour, including the use of extreme verbal language, offensive questions or statements, stalking, physical violence or sexual assault. Sexual harassment is a continuous, unwelcome sexual assault, and refusal may cause harm to the victim. Harassment is often repeated, but not always.

p71.original: 父母公开羞辱孩子：一些父母利用社交媒体上的图片和语音信息，让孩子为他们认为可耻的行为感到羞耻。照片中有被父母剪掉长发的青少年，或者在街上举着标语，上面写着：“我是骗子和小偷”“我正走向失败之路”，等等（Time，The View，July6-13，2015，pp.27-28）。
p71.en: Parents publicly humiliate their children: some use pictures and voice messages in social media to shame children for what they think is shameful. Photos of young people with long hair cut off by their parents, or carrying slogans on the street, which read: “I am a liar and thief”, “I am on the road to failure”, etc. (Time, The View, Jury 6-13, 2015, pp. 27-28).

p72.original: 霸凌几乎无处不在。它可以发生在任何学校，无论这个学校是资金短缺还是实力雄厚，是公立还是私立，是男女分校还是男女同校，是保守的还是激进的。它可以发生在课堂内外，也可以出现在工作场所或网络上。男孩和女孩都是霸凌的对象。在大多数情况下，男孩欺负其他男孩，女孩欺负其他女孩。正如《防霸凌：帮助孩子应对戏弄和霸凌的六个秘密》（Bully Blocking: Six Secrets to Help Children Deal with Teasing and Bullying）的作者伊芙琳·菲尔德（Evelyn Field，2007）所解释的那样：
p72.en: Bullying is almost everywhere. It can happen in any school, whether it is underfunded or powerful, public or private, gender-segregated or coeducational, conservative or radical. It can take place inside and outside the classroom, or in the workplace or on the Internet. Boys and girls are the target of bullying. In most cases, boys bullying other boys and girls bullying other girls. As Evelyn Field, an author of the six secrets of Bullying: Helping Children to Deal with Scraps and Bullying, explains:

p73.original: 霸凌是一种游戏，一些孩子会经常滥用他们的权力。霸凌者会在每年年初“疯狂抢购”霸凌对象，寻找合适的目标……男孩经常使用霸凌手段来获得声誉，女孩这样做则是为了保护自己的声誉。男孩往往属于等级分明的大部落，他们通常会公然欺负他人，而且更喜欢身体上的霸凌。他们注重个人成就和行动，非常勇猛有力。他们对戏弄、排斥和间接霸凌（女孩喜欢的策略）的兴趣不大。
p73.en: Bullying is a game, and some children often abuse their power. The bulldozers “crazy-buying” bullies at the beginning of each year to find the right target... Boys often use bullying to gain their reputation, and girls do so to protect their reputation. Boys are often part of a large hierarchical tribe, often openly bullying others and preferring physical bullying. Their focus on individual achievements and actions is very strong. They have little interest in bullying, exclusion and indirect bullying (girls' preferred strategies).

p74.original: 一些人认为如今的霸凌没有以前那么糟糕，现在的孩子应该“忍着点”，而另一些人则认为现在的霸凌行为太过分了。最近，由于暴力升级和一些青少年自杀事件都与网络霸凌有关，霸凌行为已成为国际关注的焦点。社交媒体研究员达纳·博伊德（Danah Boyd）说：“技术并没有从根本上改变正在发生的事情，它只是让正在发生的事情更加明显。”（Leach，2010）但我们很难否认互联网对霸凌现象的影响。由于网络的渗透性和覆盖范围以及用户的匿名性，不仅非人化变得更容易，它的影响也变得更大，甚至是致命的。
p74.en: Some believe that bullying is not as bad today as it was before, that children should be “suffering”, while others think that bullying is too much. More recently, bullying has become the focus of international attention, as violence has escalated and some youth suicides have been linked to cyberbullying. Social media researcher Dana Boyd said: “Technology does not fundamentally change what is happening, it simply makes what is happening more visible. @Leach2010: @Leach 2010 #Leach #egypt pic.twitter.com/Leach — @Leach 2010 #Jan25 (@Leach 2010) March 9, 2014 The penetration and coverage of the network and the anonymity of users not only make it easier to dehumanize, but also make its impact more significant and even fatal.

p75.original: 有趣的是，网络霸凌最早的例子是在互联网出现之前，莫妮卡·莱温斯基（Monica Lewinsky）在被曝光与她的老板——美国总统比尔·克林顿（Bill Clinton）在椭圆形办公室（Oval Office）发生性关系之后，遭到了大量的匿名辱骂。在最近的一次TED演讲（2015）中，莱温斯基生动地描述了她的羞愧和那些匿名攻击者给她带来的伤害。
p75.en: Interestingly, the first example of cyber-bullying was before the Internet, when Monica Lewinsky was exposed to a lot of anonymous insults after having had sex with her boss, United States President Bill Clinton, in Oval Office. In a recent TED address (2015), Levinsky vividly described her shame and the harm done to her by those anonymous assailants.

p77.original: 防止霸凌需要从通常的惩罚模式转变为一套对霸凌行为零容忍的系统性措施。变革的动力必须是自上而下的，从学校负责人和校长开始，其中也包括老师和家长的参与，然后推动学生自己成为变革的推动者（Kalman，2008）。研究人员丹·奥维斯（Dan Olweus，1993）在瑞典和其他斯堪的纳维亚国家采用了这样的系统变更模型，并取得了相当大的成功。在美国，那些看起来“与众不同”、更害羞、有身体残疾或同性恋的学生会受到欺负。心理学家彼得·戈德鲍姆（Peter Goldbaum）表示：“实际或感知到的性取向是学生被同学骚扰的最常见原因，并且仅次于外貌。”（Novotney，2008）打击和防止霸凌行为的新方案的核心是，从小学开始对所有年级制定促进尊重个人尊严，以及接受和容忍人类多样性的课程和实践。
p77.en: Prevention of bullying requires a shift from a common pattern of punishment to a system of zero tolerance of bullying. The driving force of change must be top-down, starting with school directors and principals, including teachers and parents, and then promoting students to become agents of change themselves (Kalman, 2008). Researcher Dan Olweus, 1993 introduced such a system change model in Sweden and other Scandinavian countries, with considerable success. In the United States, students who appear to be “discreet”, more shy, physically disabled or homosexual are bullied. According to the psychologist Peter Goldbaum, “real or perceived sexual orientation is the most common cause of student harassment and is second only to physical appearance. At the heart of the new programme to combat and prevent bullying (Novotney, 2008) is the development of curricula and practices that promote respect for the dignity of the individual and the acceptance and tolerance of human diversity at all levels, starting in primary school.

p78.original: 对于围绕目标人物形象的霸凌问题，我们主张改变这些人的自我形象和无助感。他们可以学会不再使用可能表露自己软弱、易受攻击的肢体语言，以及学习如何培养积极的自尊、新的肢体语言、有效的社交技巧及如何从同龄人那里获得更多的社会支持。格森·考夫曼（Gershen Kaufman）和他的同事们在《坚持自己：每个孩子的人格和积极的自尊心指南》（Stick Up For Yourself: Every Kid's Guide to Personal Power and Positive Self-Esteem），一书中解释说：
p78.en: We advocate changing the self-image and feelings of helplessness of the target figures in relation to bullying. They can learn to stop using language that may reveal their weakness and vulnerability, as well as to learn how to foster positive self-esteem, new body language, effective social skills and greater social support from their peers. Gershen Kaufman and his colleagues explained in the book Sticking to themselves: A Guide to each child's personality and active self-esteem (Snick Up For Yoursef: Every Kid's Guide to Personal Power and Positive Self-Esteem):

p79.original: 为了在社会上茁壮成长，积极的自尊心是我们可以培养的最重要的心理技能。拥有自尊意味着为自己感到自豪，并从内心体验到这种自豪感。没有自尊，孩子们会怀疑自己，屈服于同辈的压力，感到自己毫无价值或低人一等……有了自尊心，孩子们的内心会被更多的安全感包裹，更愿意承担积极的风险，更有可能为自己的行为负责，能够应对生活的变化和挑战，并在面对拒绝、失望、失败和挫折时保持韧性。
p79.en: In order to thrive in society, active self-esteem is the most important psychological skill we can develop. Having self-esteem means being proud of yourself and feeling that pride from within. Without self-esteem, children are skeptical, succumb to peer pressure, feel worthless or inferior... With self-esteem, children are more secure, more willing to take positive risks, more likely to be responsible for their actions, more able to cope with changes and challenges in their lives, and to remain resilient in the face of rejection, disappointment, failure and frustration.

p80.original: 需要注意的是，自尊不应与傲慢、轻蔑或自大相混淆。拥有积极自尊的人不依赖别人对他们的看法，因为他们对自己的价值充满信心，乐于做自己。
p80.en: It should be noted that self-esteem should not be confused with arrogance, contempt or arrogance. Those who have active self-esteem do not depend on what others think of them, because they have confidence in their values and are happy to be themselves.

p81.original: 从历史上看，人们认为恃强凌弱者有各种各样的心理健康缺陷，但新的研究显示，他们的社会动力学机制截然不同。许多人霸凌他人，并以此作为在同龄人中提升社会等级的一种手段。在学校中，大多数恃强凌弱的情况发生在社会地位处于中等至较高水平的学生中，不会发生在最高或最低的地位级别。一个由社会学家组成的研究小组对大约3700名初二到高二年级的美国学生进行了为期一学年的追踪调查，确定了社会攻击行为，并将其与社会地位指标联系起来（Faris & Felmlee，2011）。攻击行为指意图在身体或情感上造成伤害或痛苦的活动，每个学生都被要求列出5个他们曾刻薄对待或欺负过的学生。地位取决于一个学生在交友网络中的核心程度，在这个网络中，每个学生都需要提名5个最好的朋友。那些地位最高的人没有必要欺负任何人，而那些地位最低的人也没有社会力量来实现自己的侵略性。有关霸凌的更多信息，读者可自行上网搜索。
p81.en: Historically, the bullying is considered to have a wide range of mental health deficiencies, but new research shows that their social dynamics are very different. Many are bullying others as a means of raising social hierarchies among their peers. In schools, the majority of bullying occurs among students with a middle to higher social status and does not occur at the highest or lowest level. A study team of sociologists conducted a year-long follow-up survey of approximately 3,700 American students in grades 2 to 2, identifying social attacks and linking them to social status indicators (Faris & Felmlee, 2011). An assault is an activity intended to cause bodily or emotional harm or suffering, and each student is required to list five students who have treated or bullied him or her. Status depends on the core of a student's network of friends, where each student is required to nominate five best friends. Those with the highest status have no need to bully anyone, and those with the lowest status have no social strength to achieve their aggressive nature. Readers can search online for more information about bullying.

p82.original: 心理学很有用 运用心理学来学习心理学
p82.en: Psychology is useful. Use psychology to learn psychology.

p83.original: 你可能会将说服与广告及政治联系起来，但说服并不仅限于此。它涉及人类的所有互动交流，包括课堂上的思想沟通。在那里，你的老师和同学会试图用合理的论点说服你，他们也希望你以同样的方式阐述自己的观点。但是，社会心理学家罗伯特·西奥迪尼（Robert Cialdini，2001）表示，除了思想和意见的公开交流外，还有其他一些更微妙的说服压力值得你注意。如果你不了解这些信息，你就有可能让他人替你形成你的观点。让我们回顾一下你在读大学期间会遇到的三种微妙的影响形式。
p83.en: You may link persuasion to advertising and politics, but persuasion is not limited to that. It involves all interactions between human beings, including the communication of ideas in the classroom. There, your teachers and your fellow students tried to convince you with reasonable arguments, and they wanted you to express your views in the same way. However, according to the social psychologist Robert Cialdini, 2001, there are other more subtle pressures of persuasion than the open exchange of ideas and opinions that deserve your attention. If you don't get this information, you'll have the possibility of having someone put your mind in your head. Let us recall the three subtle forms of influence that you will encounter while going to university.

p85.original: 讲座和教科书中充斥着权威人物。例如，本书中每个括号里的注释都引用了权威人物的研究。大部分都是为了说服你，让你相信这个论点是可信的。当然，问题在于观点并不仅仅因为某位权威人物这样说就是正确的。例如，就在几年前，每一本心理学教科书都告诉我们，人类出生后其大脑不会产生新的神经元。现在，由于最新的研究，我们知道了这些教科书及其引用的专家的观点是错误的。但是，要真正证明这些主张，就需要通过科学方法获得更为客观的证据，而不仅仅是权威的说法。
p85.en: The lectures and textbooks are filled with authoritative figures. For example, each bracketed note in this book refers to the study of authoritative persons. Mostly to convince you that this argument is credible. The point, of course, is not just that one authority is right to say that. For example, just a few years ago, every psychological textbook told us that human beings were born without new neurons in their brains. Now, as a result of the latest research, we know that these textbooks and the opinions of the experts they cite are wrong. However, to truly prove these claims, more objective evidence, not just authoritative statements, is required by scientific means.

p87.original: 虽然你可能会因为朋友都喜欢而去看一部受欢迎的电影，但随大流并不能作为你在课堂上评判各种观点的好方式。许多被抛弃的思想几乎都曾被所有人接受。在心理学中，这些错误的观念包括：我们只使用了10%的大脑，人格是由生命的前两年决定的，智商测试则是衡量先天能力的良好方法。因此，与其轻易地接受你所听到和读到的内容，不如对人们普遍接受的理念提出质疑，这是一种好习惯。实际上，大多数著名科学家的职业生涯都建立在挑战其他人都接受的观点之上。
p87.en: Although you might go to a popular movie because your friends like it, it's not a good way for you to judge views in class. Many of the ideas that have been abandoned have been almost accepted by all. In psychology, these misconceptions include that we use only 10 per cent of the brain, that the personality is determined by the first two years of life, and that IQ tests are a good measure of congenital ability. It is therefore a good habit to question widely accepted ideas rather than simply accept what you have heard and read. In fact, the careers of most prominent scientists are based on challenging the views that others accept.

p89.original: 西奥迪尼说，在广告业中，阻碍竞争对手的一种好方法是发出让人们质疑对手信誉的信息。然后，为了让人们记住你所说过的话，可以使用“寄生虫”感染对手——一种记忆联系，它可以让人们在每次听到对手的声音时，就会想起你说过的话（Brookhart，2001）。一个典型的例子就是禁烟广告，这些广告看起来像万宝路的商业广告，只是它们的特色是一个咳嗽、病态的“万宝路男人”。在讲座或教科书中，你可能会遇到这种“毒寄生虫”论点，试图让某人的想法受到嘲笑。这并不一定是坏事：在学术界，说服力不强的观点会消失。但是这种技巧会变得卑鄙且有欺诈性，其中涉及对对手观点的歪曲或过度简化。要解决这个问题就要对嘲弄保持警惕，并亲自查证相反的论点。
p89.en: In the advertising industry, one of the good ways to discourage competitors was to send a message that called into question their credibility. Then, in order for people to remember what you said, the word “pathworm” can be used to infect the opponent — a memory link that reminds people of what you said every time they hear the opponent's voice (Brookhart, 2001). A typical example is smoke-free advertising, which looks like Marlboro commercials, but they are characterized by a cough, sick Man of Marlboro. In lectures or textbooks, you may encounter this “drug parasite” argument and try to make someone's thoughts laugh. This is not necessarily a bad thing: in the academic world, the less persuasive point of view disappears. However, such techniques can become despicable and fraudulent, involving distortions or excessive simplification of the views of the counterparty. To solve this problem, we need to be vigilant about mockery and to personally examine the contrary arguments.

p90.original: 当然，说服的社会心理学所涉及的内容比我们在这里讨论的要多得多。西奥迪尼（2007）的著作《影响力》（The Psychclogy of Persuasion）中可以找到更广泛的信息。而且，如果你想让自己更有说服力，试试阅读《说服力：说服他人的50个秘密》（Yes! 50 Scientifically Proven Ways to be Persuasive，Goldstein et al，2008）。也许最重要的观点是，知道一些说服的知识可以帮助你对抗在课堂内外遇到的想说服你的人，当你知道说服者（作为“有影响力的专家”）所使用的伎俩时，你就不太可能将钱捐给你不关心的事，买一辆你不喜欢的汽车，或者在无严格的审查证据的情况下接受一个理论。
p90.en: Of course, social psychology is much more involved than we are discussing here. More extensive information can be found in The Psychcology of Impact, the work of The Theodori (2007). And if you want to make yourself more persuasive, try to read Convince: 50 Secrets to Convince others! 50 Scientificly Proven Ways to be Persuasive, Goldstein et al., 2008). Perhaps the most important point is that knowing the knowledge of persuasion can help you to confront those who try to convince you, both inside and outside the classroom, when you know the trick used by the persuasionr (as an “influencing expert”), it is unlikely that you will donate money to something you don't care about, buy a car that you don't like, or accept a theory without rigorous scrutiny of evidence.

p91.original: 批判性思维的应用：恐怖主义是“疯狂的狂热分子犯下的毫无意义的暴力行为”吗
p91.en: Application of critical thinking: Is terrorism “a senseless act of violence perpetrated by fanatics”

p92.original: 2001年9月11日在美国及之后发生的恐怖袭击，以及后来发生在以色列、伊拉克、英国、西班牙、突尼斯、法国、马里、埃及和世界其他地方的自杀式炸弹袭击，都引发了一系列难以回答的问题。恐怖主义实际上与心理学有关。它通常涉及以网络方式运作的小部分群体，他们对较大的人群采取突然的暴力行动，目的是在这些人群中传播对死亡的恐惧，并引起人们对政府是否有能力保护他们的焦虑和不确定。恐怖分子并不会像传统战争那样征服其他国家，而是通过让敌人害怕成为随意袭击的牺牲品来征服敌人的思想。最近的热门视频（2015）显示，恐怖组织会将无辜受害者斩首或关在笼子里活活烧死，以宣传他们的价值观，他们在全球都臭名昭著。
p92.en: The terrorist attacks in the United States of America on 11 September 2001 and thereafter, as well as the subsequent suicide bombings in Israel, Iraq, Britain, Spain, Tunisia, France, Mali, Egypt and other parts of the world, raised a series of difficult questions. Terrorism is actually psychological. It usually involves small segments of the population operating on a network basis, who act suddenly and violently against larger groups, with the aim of spreading fear of death among them and causing anxiety and uncertainty as to the ability of the Government to protect them. Terrorists do not conquer other nations as they have done in traditional wars, but rather the idea of conquering the enemy by fearing that it will be the victim of random attacks. The recent hot video (2015) shows that terrorist organizations will decapitate or burn innocent victims alive in cages in order to promote their values, which are notorious globally.

p94.original: 全球恐怖主义是许多国家在未来几年必须面对的不断升级的威胁。恐怖分子在组织程度各异的网络中开展活动，但他们不是一个民族或国家。反恐战争是一场不对称的战争，是国家对没有集体或指定主权领地的个人的战争。他们的战术是打了就跑，随机发动进攻，这放大了他们的破坏性力量。
p94.en: Global terrorism is an escalating threat that many countries will have to face in the coming years. Terrorists operate in networks of varying degrees of organization, but they are not a people or a State. The war against terrorism is an asymmetrical war and a war by States against individuals who do not have collective or designated sovereign territories. Their tactics of hitting and running and launching random attacks magnify their destructive power.

p95.original: 你需要考虑一些关键问题：反恐战争怎样才算“赢”？如果没有一个恐怖分子领导人投降，胜利会是怎样的？应对这一全球性挑战的最佳策略，为什么是国际合作和情报资源共享，而不是一些主要国家采取单方面行动？产生如此多恐怖分子的渠道是什么？从什么意义上说，通过赢得那些可能被招募进入恐怖组织或者被训练成为自杀式炸弹袭击的年轻人的心和思想，便能够减少恐怖主义的威胁吗？
p95.en: You need to consider some key questions: What is a “win” in the war on terror? What would be the victory of a terrorist leader if he did not surrender? Why should international cooperation and the sharing of intelligence resources be the best strategies to address this global challenge, rather than unilateral actions by some major States? What are the channels for generating so many terrorists? In what sense can the threat of terrorism be reduced by winning the hearts and minds of young people who may be recruited into terrorist organizations or trained to become suicide bombers?

p96.original: 我们应该提出哪些批判性思维问题？
p96.en: What critical thinking questions should we ask?

p97.original: 产生恐怖主义暴行的原因有很多，并且很复杂。但是，媒体所宣称的原因试图简化这一问题的复杂性并降低模糊性。他们常常夸大观众和听众的恐惧。“只要流血，就可以成为头条”是一个经典说法，说明了什么才能成为电视新闻的头条（Breckenridge & Zimbardo，2006）。当媒体或公众不了解某些内容时，就可以将其标记为“无意义的”。这只意味着对他们没有意义，或者没有确凿的证据证明其背后的动机。例如，破坏公物被认为是“无意义的”，直到人们发现这是由那些试图对社会造成影响的一无所有者做的，当他们无法做出更具建设性的影响时，就会采用破坏性的、引人注目的做法。作为公民和批判性思想者，我们需要呼吁政治家、教育家、新闻工作者以及其他可能试图为复杂问题给予简单回答的人提供更好的信息。
p97.en: The causes of terrorist atrocities are many and complex. However, the reasons asserted by the media were an attempt to simplify the complexity of the issue and reduce ambiguity. They often exaggerate the fears of the audience and the audience. “Bleeding is the headline” is a classic term for what can become the headline of television news (Breckenridge & Zimbardo, 2006). When the media or the public are not aware of certain content, it can be marked as “irrelevance”. This means only that it has no meaning for them or that there is no conclusive evidence of the motives behind it. For example, destruction of public goods is considered “irrelevance” until it is discovered that it is done by those who have no ownership who seek to have an impact on society, and when they are unable to make a more constructive impact, destructive and visible practices are used. As citizens and critical thinkers, we need to appeal to politicians, educators, journalists and others who might try to provide better information for simple answers to complex questions.

p98.original: 观点是合理的还是极端的？
p98.en: Is the point of view reasonable or extreme?

p99.original: 这显然是对复杂的社会、政治、文化问题的极端概括和简化。不幸的是，最容易、最简单的反应是妖魔化那些作恶的人，但这仅仅是人身攻击，我们应该抵制这种反应，应该了解导致这些恶行的因素，而不是为它们找借口。正如我们在米尔格拉姆和斯坦福监狱的研究中看到的，仅仅是人身攻击就使我们对导致普通人做出侵略行为的情境力量视而不见。更重要的是，它让我们无法应对滋生暴力的局面。给他人贴上“邪恶”或“病态”的标签，这通常会阻止人们理解其行为的原因，只是把他们当成轻蔑或鄙视的对象。同样，将暴力和恐怖主义视为“无意义的”也是错误的。相反，从犯罪者的视角来看，破坏性行为总是有意义的。正如莎士比亚笔下的哈姆雷特所说，疯狂也有理性：如果我们要威慑潜在恐怖分子的行为，就必须了解他们的心中的理性想法。
p99.en: This is clearly an extremely broad and simplified picture of complex social, political and cultural issues. Unfortunately, the easiest and simplest response is to demonize those who commit evil, but it is only a physical attack. We should resist such a reaction and understand the factors that lead to those evils, not justify them. As we have seen in our research at Milgram and Stanford prisons, physical attacks alone blind us to the forces that lead to the acts of aggression of ordinary people. More importantly, it prevents us from coping with situations that breed violence. To label others as “evil” or “pathic”, which often prevents people from understanding the reasons for their behaviour, simply treating them as objects of contempt or contempt. Likewise, it is wrong to regard violence and terrorism as “irrelevance”. On the contrary, destructive behaviour always makes sense from the perspective of the perpetrators. As Shakespeare's Hamlet put it, madness is also rational: if we are to deter the behaviour of potential terrorists, we must understand the rational thinking in their hearts.

p101.original: 《纽约时报》记者莎拉·克肖（Sarah Kershaw，2010）在一篇详尽的报告中总结了近年来人们自杀和杀害无辜旁观者的动机。研究表明，偏见、从众、挫败、威胁或自尊心受伤的情况可能诱发攻击性行为（Aronson，2004；Baumeister et al，1996；Hassan，1998/2015）。没有证据表明恐怖分子，甚至是自杀式炸弹袭击者是病态的。相反，他们充满了愤怒，渴望报复社会的不公。他们通常受过良好的教育，关系稳定，并且有男有女。在许多情况下，他们会接受系统化训练，学习必要的技能，以有效摧毁他们认为的敌人，并为自己认为公正的事业而牺牲（Merari，2006）。
p101.en: Sarah Kershaw, a New York Times journalist, summarized in a detailed report the motives behind suicides and the killing of innocent bystanders in recent years. Studies have shown that prejudice, accompaniment, frustration, threats or self-esteem injuries can trigger aggressive behaviour (Aronson, 2004); Baumeister et al., 1996; Hassan, 1998/15. There is no evidence that terrorists, even suicide bombers, are pathological. On the contrary, they are filled with anger and desire to retaliate against social injustice. They are usually well educated, stable and have both men and women. In many cases, they are systematically trained to acquire the necessary skills to effectively destroy what they believe to be enemies and to sacrifice what they believe is just (Merri, 2006).

p102.original: 自2012年以来，新的恐惧组织ISIS的势力迅速发展，吸引了约5000名武装分子加入。他们的招聘策略主要是运用复杂的社交媒体。在Twitter上，至少有4.6万个与ISIS有关的Twitter账户通过一个庞大的“粉丝”网络组织活动。在Facebook上建立朋友关系，向孤独的人表达同情，设想传教任务。然后，ISIS通过Al Hayat媒体中心（Al Hayat media Center）添加了复杂的媒体，该媒体中心针对非阿拉伯新兵制作视频、电影和电视节目，并将信息传递到不同的国家，如德国、英国或法国。媒体是他们攻击西方异教徒的信息渠道，而许多年轻人都相信了这一点（Time magazine，p.10，July5-13，2015.）。
p102.en: Since 2012, the new fear organization ISIS has grown rapidly, attracting some 5,000 armed elements. Their recruitment strategy is based on the use of complex social media. On Twitter, at least 46,000 ISIS-related Twitter accounts were organized through a large “crowding” network. Create friends on Facebook, express sympathy to the lonely and envisage missionary tasks. ISIS then added complex media through the Al Hayat Media Center, which produces video, film and television programmes for non-Arab recruits and transmits information to different countries, such as Germany, the United Kingdom or France. The media are the channel through which they attack Western heretics, which many young people believe (Time Magazine, p. 10, July 5-13, 2015.

p103.original: 另一项分析认为，许多自杀式恐怖分子通常不是激进分子；相反，恐怖组织招募的是那些他们认为不快乐、受到伤害、想死的年轻男女。讽刺的是，人们对传统自杀的耻辱感很强烈（Lankford，2013）。
p103.en: According to another analysis, many suicide terrorists are usually not militants; On the contrary, terrorist organizations recruit young men and women who they consider unhappy, hurt and want to die. Ironically, there is a strong sense of stigma attached to traditional suicide (Lankford, 2013).

p104.original: 位于华盛顿特区的世界资源研究所（World Resources Institute）所长乔纳森·拉什（Jonathan Lash，2001）说，贫穷、无能和绝望是点燃“9·11”恐怖袭击企图的导火索。世界上有许多人生活在贫困和饥饿中，他们看不到任何希望。种族仇恨和战争加剧了他们的困境。此外，生活在这种悲惨条件下的人数正在增加，因为人口爆炸大多发生在较贫穷的国家。此外，拉什说，这些绝望的人中的大部分直接依赖于正在迅速衰竭的资源，如渔业、森林、土壤和水资源，这让情况更加不稳定。因此，每天都有成千上万的人逃离他们的家园，涌入更大、更贫穷的城市。由于第三世界的高出生率，这些人大多都是年轻人。拉什警告说，城市贫民窟里充斥着不安分、失业的年轻人，他们是“充满愤怒和绝望的火药桶，这就是为什么本·拉登（前恐怖主义头目）或其他可能追随他的人很容易招募到人的原因”。在发生于巴黎郊外贫民窟的暴力骚乱中，我们就看到了这一点，这些骚乱是由没有工作、受教育机会很少的年轻移民造成的。
p104.en: Jonathan Lash, Director of the World Resources Institute in Washington, D.C., said that poverty, incompetence and despair were the trigger for the terrorist attack of 11 September. There are many people in the world who live in poverty and hunger and who see no hope. Racial hatred and war exacerbate their plight. Moreover, the number of people living in such deplorable conditions is increasing, as most of the population explosions occur in poorer countries. In addition, Rush said that most of these desperate people were directly dependent on resources that were rapidly depleting, such as fisheries, forests, soil and water resources, which made the situation even more precarious. As a result, tens of thousands of people flee their homes every day, pouring into larger and poorer cities. Owing to the high birth rate in the third world, most of them are young people. Rush warns that the urban slums are filled with troubled, unemployed young people, who are “powder buckets of anger and despair, which is why bin Laden (former head of terrorism) or others who might follow him can easily be recruited”. We have seen this in the violent riots in the slums outside Paris, caused by young migrants who do not have jobs and have little education.

p105.original: 相关结论是否存在被偏差污染的可能？
p105.en: Is there a risk of contamination by deviation?

p106.original: 这里存在一些偏见：第一，性格偏差侧重于单个犯罪者，而忽略了其行为背景、情境以及塑造其行为并赋予其目的的系统；第二，简化偏差，将困难、复杂的问题简化为简单的术语，给人一种可以找到简单解决方案的错觉。正如我们所见，做出和接受关于恐怖主义和恐怖分子的论断的原因包括屈服于常见的谬论。打击恐怖主义需要了解导致一般人成为恐怖分子的直接因素，以及系统对个人和团体做出的这种极端决定所产生的更广泛的影响。
p106.en: (a) There are prejudices: first, gender bias focuses on individual offenders, neglecting the context, context and system that shapes their behaviour and confers its purpose; Secondly, to simplify deviations, to simplify difficult, complex issues into simple terms and to create the illusion that simple solutions can be found. As we have seen, the reasons for making and accepting assertions about terrorism and terrorists include submission to common fallacy. The fight against terrorism requires an understanding of the direct factors that lead to the general human being becoming a terrorist and the broader implications of such extreme decisions systematically taken by individuals and groups.

p107.original: 我们能够得出什么结论？

p108.original: 理解恐怖主义需要多方面的综合见解，而不仅仅是心理学方面的理解。金钱、权力、资源和长时间的积怨也必须予以考虑。世界上很多人都把美国视为敌人。要理解这种看法并以建设性的方式应对，就需要美国人从以美国为敌的一面看待这场冲突。
p108.en: Understanding terrorism requires a multifaceted and integrated vision, not just a psychological understanding. Money, power, resources and prolonged grievances must also be taken into account. Many people around the world see the United States as an enemy. Understanding this view and responding constructively require Americans to look at the conflict from the opposite side of the United States.

p109.original: 我们还必须认识到，恐怖主义并不总是涉及国际冲突。想一想科伦拜恩高中（Columbine High）和弗吉尼亚理工大学（Virginia Tech University）的枪击事件，2011年初在亚利桑那州图森市（Tucson，Arizona）发生的大规模杀害和伤害无辜平民的事件，以及近年来针对LGBT个人的袭击、成千上万的种族仇恨犯罪，针对堕胎提供者的暴力事件频频成为新闻的头条（Doyle，2001）。不要错误地认为恐怖主义永远是外来威胁。尽管有些文化比其他文化更暴力，但每一种文化都可能滋生暴力恐怖分子，这些人会恐吓其他人（Moghaddam et al，1993；Shiraev & Levy，2001）。请记住，炸毁俄克拉何马城联邦大楼、杀害数百名无辜民众的炸弹袭击者是一位名叫蒂莫西·麦克维（Timothy McVeigh）的美国恐怖分子。三K党（Ku Klux Klan）是美国独有的恐怖组织，以暴力的方式向黑人和其他被他们视为敌人的人灌输敬畏和恐惧。2015年，在南卡罗来纳州查尔斯顿一个黑人教堂的祈祷仪式上，一名年轻男子杀害了9名去教堂做礼拜的人，这应该被视为恐怖分子，尤其是在接下来的几周内，因为他的仇恨犯罪引发了美国南方另外六个黑人教堂的焚毁。
p109.en: We must also recognize that terrorism does not always involve international conflicts. Consider the shootings at Columbine High and Virginia Tech University of Technology, the mass killing and wounding of innocent civilians in Tucson, Arizona, in early 2011, and the attacks on LGBT individuals in recent years, the thousands of hate crimes, and the frequent rise of violence against abortion providers as news headlines (Doyle, 2001). Terrorism must not be mistakenly perceived as an external threat. Although some cultures are more violent than others, each culture may breed violent terrorists who intimidate others (Moghaddam et al., 1993); Shiraev & Levy, 2001. Remember that the bomber who blew up the federal building in Oklahoma City and killed hundreds of innocent people was an American terrorist named Timothy McVeigh. The Ku Klux Klan, a unique terrorist organization in the United States, has violently inculcated fear and fear among the blacks and others whom they regard as enemies. In 2015, at a prayer ceremony at a black church in Charleston, South Carolina, a young man killed nine people who went to church to worship, which should be regarded as terrorists, especially in the coming weeks, as his hate crime triggered the burning of six other black churches in the south of the United States.

p110.original: 我们已经看到了敌人，很可能是我们，也很可能是他们。
p110.en: We have seen the enemy, probably us, and possibly them.

p112.original: 对于一个主要关注好人如何变坏的章节，最好的结尾莫过于留给你一段关于人类团结和尊重彼此的精彩陈述。它出自诗人约翰·多恩（John Donne，Meditations XVII）：
p112.en: There is no better end to a chapter that focuses primarily on how good people get bad than a wonderful statement about human solidarity and respect for each other. It's from John Donne, Medications XVII:

p115.original: 任何人的死亡都会使我的生命流失，
p115.en: The death of any person will take my life away.

p116.original: 因为我是人类的一部分；
p116.en: Because I'm part of the human race.

p118.original: 永远不要在意丧钟为谁而鸣，
p118.en: Never mind who the bells are ringing for.

p120.original: 所以，当你有疑问时，采取道德的方式，注意情境的力量，警惕潜在的不公正的权威，对与他人和睦相处的需求保持敏感，为自己的行为承担个人责任，保持批判性思考，准备好承认你犯了一个错误（这样可以减少失调），在协作的团队中工作，警惕各种权力滥用。
p120.en: So, when you have doubts, take a moral approach, beware of the power of the situation, be wary of potential unjust authority, be sensitive to the need to live in harmony with others, take personal responsibility for your actions, be critical, be ready to admit that you have made a mistake (which can reduce the imbalance), work in a collaborative team and be wary of abuse of power.

p121.original: 最后，考虑采用一种新的“英雄想象”，将你对他人的同情心转变为对他们有帮助的英勇行动，只要你准备好站起来，大声说出来，并在生活中面临挑战时采取明智而有效地行动，就会让世界变得更美好。
p121.en: Finally, consider adopting a new “heroes imagination” to transform your compassion for others into heroic action that will help them, and that will make the world a better place if you are ready to stand up, speak out and act wisely and effectively when the challenges of life are faced.

p122.original: 为自己考虑一个新的社会角色：“在训练中，我会成为一名平凡的英雄。”
p122.en: Think of a new social role for myself: “In training, I will be a common hero.
